column1: # P4-139 criterion 3 — enforcement inventory for saturating arithmetic.
# Saturating a value that SIZES OR BOUNDS A MEMORY REGION turns an overflow
# into usize::MAX, which is the worst possible value to then hand an allocator
# or a slice constructor. Every such site has been converted to checked
# arithmetic with a typed error; this file pins the ones that remain, each of
# which saturates something that is NOT a memory span.
# `tests/sizing_arithmetic_gate.rs` fails if this file and the sources
# disagree, so a NEW saturating expression cannot appear without a human
# classifying it. That is the mechanism criterion 3 asks to name: a test, not a
# grep or a review checklist, because a test runs on every CI leg.
# deliberately excluded — it is the IDCT's C-parity idiom at 244 sites, where
# wrapping is the specified behaviour being matched. That narrows the
# criterion's literal wording and is recorded as such in P4-139.
#   value-saturation    clamping a sample/pixel value; saturation IS the intent
#   counter             a monotonic counter; saturation is a graceful cap
#   bounds-check        saturating high makes the check FAIL, the safe direction
#   geometry-count      MCU/block/restart counts, not byte spans
#   capacity-growth     growth hint already bounded by an explicit .min(cap)
#   clamped-difference  a - b floored at 0, where 0 is the correct answer
